Each nonself private port has one segment; parallel original endpoints never share a private port. REVERSED is bookkeeping on the already swapped current edges, not evidence of a current backward edge. The selected source counters, neighborhoods and orthogonal route algorithms read current endpoints/ports/geometry/priorities, not the REVERSED flag. CYCLIC appears in the fixed worker only as a property declaration and writes, not a later-stage read. Do not clear either flag to force old guards.

With n<=8/m<=28 and normalized ranks<=7, split nodes<=176, segments<=196, ports<=392 and layers<=8. The inherited full default loops/trees/queues/counters have no branch limited to64; indices, degrees, marks and at most196^2 segment crossing/count combinations stay exactly within signed32. Float coordinates, source tie ordering and every RNG operation remain as in the inherited full kernels. The old simple-DAG combinatorial56 lemma is not used. The196 bound is for original split LEdges, not routing-private HyperEdgeSegments. For each layer boundary each raw nonself edge crosses at most once, giving at most28 initial routing segments; critical splitting creates at most one partner per initial segment, so at most56 temporary segments per boundary (392 is a conservative total across7 internal boundaries). Even this larger private bound leaves all signed32 counters exact. Do not reuse196 as an unjustified global private-segment bound.

Only empty-adjacency NORTH ports survive loopRestorer; all live ordinary edges still use EAST/WEST and adjacent layers. Source getPorts_0 is an ordered side/type filter, not portSideIndices. Horizontal placement counts ports with nonempty incoming/outgoing so late empty NORTH ports contribute zero to ratio. Do not invent cache validity or nonnegative internalY constraints. Keep full routing dependency/split/slot/numeric/RNG algorithms and real loop-expanded margins. SELF_LOOPS selects separately configured pre/post processors; late NORTH does not add compile-time NORTH_SOUTH_PORTS flag or enable another ordinary routing mode.
